_meta.description: Item pool for the second normative-dimension stability/recognition task. Replaces the emoji/THINGS memory probe in its entirety. Domain A is always included in domain sampling; two further domains are sampled at random from B, D, E, F.
_meta.row_sampling_rule: for each selected domain, row_tested = random.choice(domain_rows)

foil_rule.similar: the untested side of the same row_tested (same topic, different statement)
foil_rule.foil_pair: both sides of one additional row, randomly drawn from the SAME domain as the tested row (excluding the tested row itself). Foils are same-domain, not cross-domain: drawing the foil from an unselected domain let participants solve the trial by topic-exclusion (recognizing they were never asked about that domain at all) rather than by recalling the specific statement. Foils also now come as a matched pair (both sides of their row), not a single lone statement, so the recognition screen presents two structurally symmetric pairs (target+similar vs foil_a+foil_b) rather than one real pair against one obviously unrelated odd-one-out.

_meta.test_format: Blocked sequence, not per-item interleaved: (1) claimed_recall_step1 asked first; (2) framing_recall asked only if claimed_recall_step1 == 'Yes'; (3) recognition test for all 3 items, 4AFC per item (target / similar / foil_a / foil_b, order randomized, all same domain) plus a 5th 'I don't remember' option shown separately below the four statements, run BEFORE any reveal, so recognition is never contaminated by feedback; (4) reveal screen shows all 3 correct target statements together, with no right/wrong feedback on the recognition answers; (5) re-measurement for all 3 items, now based on the revealed (confirmed) statements; (6) redistribution-study frequency question is appended to the final survey block, not the memory task itself.

backend_variables.sides_tested: array of 3 objects {row_id, side, item_id, item_text}
backend_variables.foils_new: map row_id -> {domain, row_id_source, side, item_id, item_text}
backend_variables.phase2_recognition: map row_id -> {presented_order: [item_id,...], choice: item_id | null, classification: 'target'|'similar'|'foil_a'|'foil_b'|'dont_remember', correct: bool, rt_ms: int}
backend_variables.claimed_recall_step1: bool (did they claim to remember doing the redistribution elicitation)
backend_variables.framing_recall_correct: bool, computed against participant's actual assigned Phase-1 framing

claimed_recall_step1.wording: Do you remember completing an earlier exercise in this study where you indicated your views about income redistribution?

framing_recall.wording: To the best of your memory, was that earlier exercise based on luck or based on performance/skill?
framing_recall.scoring_note: framing_recall_correct = (framing_recall_response matches participant's actual assigned Phase-1 framing); 'I don't remember' scored as incorrect/missing, not as a third category, unless analyzed separately.

redistribution_study_frequency.wording: Excluding our studies, how often have you participated in studies in which you were asked to redistribute money, or to give your opinion on redistribution?
redistribution_study_frequency.placement_note: Belongs to the final survey block, not the memory/stability task itself; asked once, after the recognition test and re-measurement are complete.
